A comeback for the ages: Trump's influence on Huang's return to NvidiaByBernd Debusmann Jr, White House reporter and Kali Hays, Technology reporter, Reporting fromSan FranciscoPublished23 November 2026Updated 1 hour ago
Nvidia has reinstated CEO Jensen Huang just days after rejecting his offer to return to the AI chipmaker - and less than two weeks after he was forced to resign over a reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
The company came under pressure by Donald Trump to reappoint Huang - and on Monday, the US president said he "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to bring him back.
But now both Trump and Nvidia are facing bipartisan backlash from lawmakers, just as Huang is due to testify before Congress next week.
The CEO's comeback helped end a week-long losing streak in US stocks that left the S&P 500 in correction territory, and added nearly $1 trillion to Nvidia's market value.
Stock prices for Nvidia fell sharply after Huang stepped down, but jumped by 31% after he was reappointed on Monday - adding about $1tn to the company's market value.
But Nvidia's closing price was still down slightly from its Friday morning opening price.
As Asian stock markets opened, Nvidia racked up more gains and helped lift other share prices across the tech sector.

item.title: [BBC World] Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
Nato chief Mark Rutte and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz respond to reports of Russian plans to launch nuclear weapons into spaceByHelen DavidsonPublished3 hours ago
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after reports that Russia was preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.
Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media outlets. It was not clear which country had authored the reports.
Asked about the reports, Rutte said: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element."
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he hadn't seen the latest reports but dismissed reports citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously".
The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign".
Rutte told the press conference in Berlin that Nato had a variety of response options.
"When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary," he said.
Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, the reports by broadcasters NDR and WDR, and newspaper Sueddeutsche Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead. It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites.
Standing alongside Rutte, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz did not confirm or deny the reports of Russia's plans, but said they "reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue".

TORONTO -- The Pentagon accused Canada on Monday of falling short as a credible partner in defending North America, delivering a sharp rebuke to its longtime ally over military spending and its reconsideration of American-made F-35 fighter jets.
In an unusually blunt fact sheet, the Defense Department accused Ottawa of failing to make the tough decisions needed to modernize its military and meet NATO commitments.

The criticism follows a classified directive from U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth that Republican U.S. Sen. item.title: [BBC World] US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesByKali HaysTechnology reporterPublished23 November 2026
The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America.
The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US.
The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang.
The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China.
When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed.
Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang.
Alice Huang (no relation) was thought by US intelligence to be working as an asset for Beijing, creating national security concerns within the US.
China has denied that she is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.
On 12 November, Jensen Huang resigned after allegations he had had another affair, this one with a Nvidia employee.
On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstated him after US President Donald Trump said he had "convinced" the company and "made the deal".
The commerce department has said it had been investigating Megaspeed for almost two years.
The department said it had suspected the company was violating US export controls by helping to get Nvidia's chips into the hands of companies within China.

item.description:
Hungary’s Magyar says he will visit Ukraine in a sign of mending relations
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar plans to visit Ukraine soon, signaling improved relations between the two countriesByJUSTIN SPIKE Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 9:49 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BUDAPEST, Hungary -- Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said Monday that he will soon travel to Ukraine in a sign that the icy relations between the two neighboring countries, pushed to the breaking point by former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, are improving.
Magyar's planned visit to the embattled country comes after Kyiv passed a law in October — long demanded by Hungary’s government — that expanded language rights for a Hungarian ethnic minority in western Ukraine.
Speaking to lawmakers on Monday, Magyar did not announce a date for his visit, but said it would take place in the western Ukrainian region of Zakarpattia, home to tens of thousands of ethnic Hungarians. It will be the first visit to the region by a Hungarian head of government since 2015.
Magyar denounced Russian strikes that hit the mountainous region last week and said he would travel there “soon ... to personally deliver the support of the motherland to our Hungarian brethren.”
Before Magyar and his Tisza party won a landslide election in April, Hungary's government under Orbán pursued a hostile approach to Ukraine, repeatedly blocking aid to Kyiv and holding up European Union sanctions against Russia, all while maintaining cordial ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Orbán's government had also depicted Ukraine as a threat to Hungary's security, and cast President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as an enemy, using his likeness in taxpayer-funded political campaigns.

Indonesian rescuers race to find 34 missing workers after a deadly candy factory fire
Indonesian rescuers are searching for 34 missing workers after a deadly fire swept through a candy factory west of JakartaByNINIEK KARMINI Associated PressNovember 23, 2026, 1:26 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
JAKARTA, Indonesia -- Indonesian rescuers searched Monday for 34 missing workers after a deadly fire swept through a candy factory west of Jakarta.
Saturday’s fire broke out at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Banten province. Firefighters battled flames for about 14 hours before largely containing the blaze tearing through the three-story building.
About 300 workers were inside the factory when the fire erupted, officials said. Of those, 63 were believed to have been in the hardest-hit area, mostly on the second floor where the flames originated from a cooling unit.
Indonesia’s National Search and Rescue Agency, or Basarnas, did not immediately offer a death toll, but said they collected human remains in 24 body bags for identification through forensic examination.
Meanwhile, rescuers saved 29 workers, five of whom were hospitalized, and continue to search for the missing.

Ukraine sank a Russian warship docked in Libya and disabled a cargo vessel off the North African country’s coast, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday, in Kyiv’s latest attack on Russian assets far from the front lines.
The warship — identified as the 344-foot navy corvette Merkury — was attacked with seven maritime drones, sinking the ship and destroying a combat helicopter on board, Zelensky said in a post to Telegram.

item.title: [BBC China] China issues Mount Fuji warning as family of missing climber offers reward
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
The $75,000 reward offered by Chen Jie's family has sparked fears of more reckless climbing attemptsByKelly NgPublished20 November 2026
The Chinese embassy in Japan has warned its citizens against off-season ascents of Mount Fuji amid concerns that the hefty reward offered by a missing hiker's family could encourage more reckless climbing.
Chen Jie, 25, vanished on 8 November on the mountain. His family is offering 500,000 yuan ($75,000; £57,300) to anyone who finds him alive, and 100,000 yuan to anyone who recovers his body, say Chinese and Japanese media reports.
Strong winds and blizzards pose serious risks during the closed season, especially as shelter and first-aid centres are not operational, the embassy said on Tuesday.
Mount Fuji's official climbing season runs from around early July to early September.
Earlier this year, authorities of Yamanashi province, where the northern part of Mount Fuji sits, had said that people who attempt to climb Mount Fuji during off-peak seasons and then require rescue by helicopter will have to pay for the service from next year on.
Authorities will also require those looking to scale Fuji during the off-season to submit detailed climbing plans.
"We hope that these measures will cause people to rethink what climbing Mount Fuji during the winter is like," Kotaro Nagasaki, the prefecture governor, said at the time.
On Wednesday, Nagasaki told reporters that attempts to find the missing climber could lead to "secondary disasters".
According to Japanese news outlet the Mainichi Shimbun, Nagasaki appeared to appeal to Chen's family, saying: "I understand that your family is important, but please refrain from doing anything that could endanger others."
Some social media users in Japan have similarly expressed fears would entice people to venture into the mountains ill-prepared and lead to more accidents.

item.title: [BBC China] Analysis: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance
item.description:
Image source, EPAImage caption,
The visuals of the historic trilateral meeting may be the only lasting impression left by the summitByAnthony ZurcherNorth America correspondentPublished19 November 2026
Donald Trump went into his trilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping with little on the agenda and no clear asks – and he left with little in return.
In the end, the visuals of the meeting – the "optics", as political wags like to say – may be the only lasting impression from the summit, billed by some as a historic "Yalta 2.0" meeting of great powers.
The pomp and the ceremony, in the end, may be what the US president wanted most. Trump, bruised by his Republican Party's drubbing in midterm congressional elections earlier this month, clearly relished the global spotlight during his three-day trip to Asia and the historic nature of the first-ever US-Russia-China trilateral meeting.

That might appear to be a low bar, but it's one that could satisfy the American president.
